div.head:
The Commentary of Song of Songs, that is to say,
the Hymn of Hymns and the Praise of Praises

div.ab:
Further we come to the third book of Solomon and to the consummation of his compositions and the ascent towards perfection, and this (commentary) briefly and (gleaned) from many commentators according to the version of the Septuagint with the Lord I begin. Chapter 1:2. Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, that is, the spirit says these (things) by the mouth of Solomon assuming the character of the church and of the soul that was smitten with the love of the Messiah. For she begins to desire the kisses of the bridegroom when she has heard from the prophets that he is about to come and espouse her. The kisses are his words, his precepts, the union with him, the love for him. Because thy breasts are better than wine, that is, the breasts are the two Testaments and the milky teaching which is in them, by which the soul is reared until it is lifted up to the wisdom that is discussed among the perfect, that which is better than all the rational and natural wisdom of the philosophers with which many are drunk. For this reason he compares it to wine. (v.3) And the smell of thine ointments
is more excellent than all the aromas, that is, your knowledge, your virtues, your precepts, are exalted above all the aromas; that is to say, the human sciences and those virtues which were praised from of old, but for which the recompense of the eternal world had not been revealed. Thy name is ointment poured forth, that is, your nature which is incomprehensible; by names, however, which are derived from your works you are known, that is, from your creations and every one of them into which your wisdom and your creatorship and your power is poured abundantly you are known. Again, your name is poured forth in your apostles and your teachers, and these are filled with your wisdom and with your love and your knowledge so that they might do wonders in your name. Therefore the handmaids, in other codices the young maidens, have loved thee, that is, the souls of the saints that were exalted with the knowledge of the bridegroom above the stage of youth which is shaken by all winds and yet they do not grow old with sin but are in the stage of manhood and firmness in the practice of virtues; these, indeed, being firmly set in the hopes of the groom, love him. (c.4) Draw us after thee, in other codices they drew thee after thee, that is, loving you and keeping your precepts they have drawn you to them, for by this you are drawn as you have said: Whosoever has my precepts and
keeps them I and my father come to him. (John 14:21ᵃ,23ᵇ). The King brought me into his chamber: let us rejoice and be glad in thee, that is, the souls that follow your steps and precepts and run after the knowledge and the odor of your teachings, and for this they were worthy to enter the chambers of your secrets; that is, the wisdom which is discussed among the perfect, the revelation, the Kingdom, in which they rejoice as in the bridegroom himself. We will love thy breasts more than wine, that is, the abundance of your teachings in the old and new (Testaments) more than all the teaching of the pagans. Righteousness loved thee, that is, he that is just and righteous is the very one who loves you, that is the angels, the apostles, the just, the righteous. (v.5) Black am I but beautiful, that is, the soul says these (words); that is to say, the church that was turned from error to truth: I was black with sin, with worshipping idols, but when I clove to the bridegroom he made me beautiful with baptism. And she encourages everyone who is black with sin, that they should not be afraid of approaching the bridegroom, the Messiah; he is not ashamed of their blackness, but he whitens them with the ablution (i.e., baptism) and makes them beautiful. Ye daughters of Jerusalem, that is,the souls from Israel and from the
gentiles that became disciples he calls daughters, and because by them the church perceived by the mind and by the senses is to be inhabited they are consequently called daughters of Jerusalem. As the tents of Kedar, that is, those of whom David says: Woe to me that my sojourning was prolonged and I dwelt in the tents of Kedar (Ps.120:5); that is to say, darkness, which are the different kinds of sin, which on account of its darkness is compared to Kedar. I was like these dark tents, but when I drew near to the groom and desired his kisses he made me like the curtain of Solomon, that is, white and bright and one that is suitable for the dwelling of the true Solomon, that is, even for that of the Messiah, he that is the peace of the upper and nether regions. Then with words which are more excellent than these she encourages those who are prepared to be brought near to discipleship, and she says: (v.6) Look not upon me, because I am darkened, because the sun has been careless of me, that is, do not think that I have blackened my soul with sin in being obedient to the devil and consequently the bridegroom does not receive me and does not make me white; nor again should you think that because the sun has been careless of me therefore I sinned; for I (sinned) of my own will and he did not lead me by force to him until I turned of my own will again; therefore if you turn like me he will whiten your blackness and the sun of righteousness will not be careless
of you. She shows the cause of sin. Again, the sun has blackened me, that is, the temptations, like that (which is written): the sun will not smite thee by day,(Psalms 121:6), and when she shone upon the earth it dried up,(Mark 4:6). My mother's sons strove with me, that is, she calls the godhead mother, the creatress of the creatures, and in whose knowledge they were conceived, and when he desired he created and brought them forth to reality. He calls the demons sons of the godhead, who strove with our nature from the beginning, that is, with Adam; and they drove him out of Paradise and caused the generation of Noah to commit whoredom; they corrupted the Sodomites and caused the whole world to worship idols. They made me keeper in the vineyard, that is, they set the human soul upon desires, upon idolatry, and upon evil thoughts. I have not kept my own vineyard, that is, Paradise, the natural law, the knowledge of God. (v.7) O thou, whom my soul loveth, cause me to know, that is, the bride is saying to the groom, the one whom she loved and after whom she went forth: Where dost thou feed the flock and where dost thou retire at noon, that is, let me know in what pastures and disciplines of virtue do you pasture those who love you, and in what places do you take rest and make such as these worthy of the noon, that is the unspeakable light of your delight, so that when you bring those (that love you) to it you might also
give me there rest with you; for I fear that if you do not do these things, lest I become, that is, I come to be like a wanderer after those among whom I pasture, and not finding you and those that belong to you, I wander after the flocks of thy companions, that is, after those demoniac heresies, which also had flocks in this world, which were led astray by their doctrine. She calls them his companions because they belonged to his adversary and left his discipleship and worship, though they knew he was their creator; for the Lord also called Judas my companion and not my disciple, because he was a companion of these and with them was not worthy of the voice of the bridegroom. The friends of the groom, that is the patriarchs, the prophets, the apostles, turn to her and say: (v.8) If thou know not thyself, fairest of women, that is, mine art thou, for you have been created in the image of God and guard yourself from all evils; and if you guard yourself from all those who are opposed to your betrothed one - the hateful sins, then verily you will be beautiful in conjunction with the groom; therefore guard this beauty. But if you do not know and keep these go forth, go thou forth in the footsteps of the flocks and feed thy kids by the shepherds' tents, that is, get yourself out from the divine fold, the heavenly shepherd, and whoever goes forth from this, walks in the footsteps of the demons; and she also feeds her kids with their teaching, that is to say, with evil thoughts, with shameful passions and with vain teachings of the former shepherds, that
is, the demons. But after such a purification and precepts and admonition she is wholly worthy of the groom; indeed, he is now the one that speaks to her and says: (v.9) To my horses in Pharaoh's chariot have I likened thee my companion, that is, the soul that contended with the demons and overcame them and did the will of the groom he compares to spiritual hosts, that is - the horses, over whom the Lord raised himself (Exod. 15:1) when he drowned the natural Pharaoh. (v.10) How beautiful are thy cheeks, like those of a dove, that is he compares the cheeks of this one to those of a dove because of its chastity since it does not cohabit with any other besides her first (mate). So also the cheeks of the soul which is adorned with chastity are compared to this, because by means of the cheeks chastity is made light of, by licentious appearance and unrestrained laughter, by shameless hints and the like. Thy neck is as necklaces, that is, that by which the head is lifted up, that is to say the mind, from the earthly things, to the end that it might look towards the heavenly and the divine, he likens to a circlet and necklace of beads; and the mind when it is encircled by virtue is lifted up from the earth and earthly things. (v.11) I will make for thee pomegranates of gold, that is, the friends of the groom say these things to her: Do not think that because you have vanquished the demons though you have not become chastened and uplifted from the earthly things that immediately you are coming to the
unity of the groom and will be with him one - he who is pure, tested gold, because he possesses incorruptibility by nature, but we will make for you pomegranates of gold with studs of silver, that is, we adorn you with divine sciences and with those presents and spiritual gifts which possess the high value of gold because they lead to that incorruptibility and show you the groom by means of them; and with studs of silver we adorn thee, (means) this, that the speech of the Lord is pure and tested silver in the earth. (v.12) Till the King came to his feast, that is, at present our King and your King, the Messiah, is reclining at the feast of his occultation with his father and is resting with the heavenly hosts; therefore these will suffice you until you will be brought unto him. But she who knows herself and knows that she is worthy of the divine gifts says: Thy spikenard gives forth its smell, that is, I am inhaling from myself the gifts of the Messiah, for I am rich with these; and not only do I smell these from myself, that is the knowledge and virtue of the Messiah, but even to others is my odor revealed and inhaled by them, as Paul also said: A sweet smell are we in the Messiah to God, (II Corinth, 2:15). (v.13) A bundle of stacte is my sister's son, that is, the Messiah to him who loves him; binding together by faith all his precepts and his knowledge; he puts these in his heart, between his breasts, that is, wherever in the mind theory and practice are potentially stored. She calls him my
sister's son because from her sister, the Godbearer (θεοτόκος) he was incarnated and born; likewise she designates him stacte, because from the sum of his sciences and his precepts he blows upon her continually a sweet smell of death and of bodily sufferings by which the garments of the groom are perfumed according to the word of David (Ps. 45:8, All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia); for those who do these things which are in their hearts openly but also keep them in private within them are not afraid of anything. (v.14) A cluster of wine blossoms is my sister's son to me, that is, the Messiah, who, having become man, like unto a grapecluster ran his course in a variety of statures in the world until he had fulfilled the dispensation; then his wine was pressed out by the crucifixion that the world may drink of it and live by it. In the same manner, now, among the recipients, he is in their hearts in the likeness of a cluster (of grapes), and little by little like the natural cluster he grows in the soul, now sprouting and then exuding its odor and presently becoming vine-buds and then attaining completion. In this case of the soul, however, which has not yet reached perfection the Messiah is to her a vine-bud; and in the vineyards of Engad, that is, in the thoughts of the recipients, in the soul of those who became disciples whom he calls vineyards that are planted in Engad, that is, in the heavenly place, in the church of God.

(v.1) I am a flower of the plain, that is, formerly I was a plain of desolation and I was without water, but when the word arose and called me I became a flower that went up from the earth and earthly (things), and there blew from me the sweet odor of the Messiah. A lily of the valleys, that is, from the depths of the world and worldly (things) and the darkness of the demons I went up by means of the faith in him, and I became a lily in splendor and in sweetness of odor. But the
Messiah says: (v.2) As a lily in the midst of thorns so is my companion among the daughters, that is, by this he teaches her that though she was resplendent and rose up in the form of a lily from the valley, yet it is not right that she should persist amidst sin which is symbolized by thorns; therefore it is right for her to take heed lest she be harmed by these. And not only of thorns, that is from sin, does he urge her to take heed, but also of the daughters, that is, of effeminate thoughts and worldly desires which he calls daughters, whose father, that is to say, their sower, is the devil. Thereupon the bride praises the groom and says: (v.3) As the apple among the trees of the wood, so is my sister's son among the daughters, that is, she calls him apple on account of his beauty which when we look at him we become beautiful. Again, because of the sweet odor that he confers upon us, and because he is to us food and drink. The trees of the wood are the men who live in this world as in a wood among the evil beasts, that is to say, the demons. But when we are sons of God and plant this apple among us we are not afraid of the beasts of the forest. I desired his shadow and sat down, that is under the faith that is in him and the keep-
ing of his precepts and doctrines I yearned (to be). His fruit was sweet in my throat, that is, his precepts are more desirable than gold and sweeter than honey. (v.4) Bring me into the wine house, that is, she asks of the angels or of the apostles and teachers that they should bring her into the wine house; that is, to the knowledge of the secrets that when he was crucified there came down from him blood and water, and also the cup that he gave he called his blood; for I desire that you should teach me, wherefore did he suffer and there came down from him blood and water and he mixed his blood with water and gave it to us. And set love before me, that is, teach me how I may love God, and with what and how I may love men and enemies. (v.5) Strengthen me with perfumes, that is, implant within me these unshakable virtues, so that by means of their stability I shall not be shaken by the evil thoughts. Stay me with apples, that is, with apples which grow in the midst of human nature, so that when I am wrapped up, that is to say, I am surrounded, with this fruit I will not inhale destructive death, and the sweet smell of this (fruit) will drive away from me the breath of these deadly (ones), likewise when I shall hunger after the worldly sciences as of old. Because I am sick with love, that is,
to such a degree was I smitten with the love of the groom, that I love that he should encompass me and surround me from all sides, and in this way I shall gladden the senses of the body and of the soul. (v.6) His left hand is under my head, that is, those faculties of his diligence by which he lifts up my head from the earthly (things); and when I am lifted up from these his right hand will embrace me; that is, he will encompass me with his right hand, that is to say, with his angelic hosts, those, when surrounding me, do not permit my mind to lean upon anything earthly, but they lift me up and bring me into the heaven with them. (v.7) I have adjured you, ye daughters of Jerusalem, that is, I adjure the patriarchs, the prophets, the apostles, and all the souls of the saints who live continually in that Jerusalem which is in heaven, that they should beg of God not to allow this love to cool, but to keep it continually till she will come to him just as they came to him. With the powers, that is to say, with those angelic hosts, those who, because they were firm in the ministrations, were the cause of their deliverance. And with the forces of the field, that is, everything by which those of this world were strengthened when they overcame the devil and sin, which they took from the field of teachings and godly seed, and were strengthened by it over the world and worldly (things). You shall not make to stand, that is, you shall not allow the love to remain in one state, but that it should advance and continually rise up until it is brought to the one who desires that
all men should live and should turn to the knowledge of truth. And he adds to that (passage) that you do not cause to stand, but stir up the love till he pleases, that is, you shall not allow the love to abate from that fever which has laid hold of it until I will have accomplished the whole desire of God. (v.8) The voice of my sister's son! behold, he leaps upon the mountains, he jumps upon the hills, that is, after these (things), the holy bride, like one that was assured by voices of the groom saying: Whosoever has my precepts with him and keeps them I and my father come to him and an abode for him, (John 14:21ᵃ, 23ᵇ) encourages, therefore, those that became her disciples not to cool their love, because he, the Messiah, is about to come to their help, that by his advent they are delivered from the war of the devil and demons, which she calls mountains and hills because of their height and wickedness, for it is through her that he leaps and jumps when she overcomes them and rises up above them and is exalted. And she compares him- (v.9) My sister's son is like the deer or the young hart, that is, because he is an exterminator of the spiritual snakes just like the deer, also the young hart; that is to say, the foal of the hart destroys perceptual snakes. Upon the mountains of Bethel, that is, the passage is concerning those men who became mountains, because they loved the virtue of God and the help of God that dwells upon them and in them; behold! the one standing behind our wall, that is, not far from us, that is, not hidden in his essence from us; and we are the cause of his standing at a distance from us and not he; looking through the windows peeping through the hinges, that is, through
his prophets, the evangelical doctrines, and the types and symbols, he now looks at the soul and the church; through these which he calls windows and hinges, from which there comes to us the light from him; through the windows as from the prophets, and through the hinges as from the apostles, who by the words of the gospels captured men, as he told them; and through these, she says, he calls her when she prays his prayer. (v.10) My sister's son replys and says to me: Rise up, come, my companion, my fair one, my dove, that is, rise up always from sin, do not abstain from continually approaching me, because when you were beautiful with the faith that is within me, also with the spiritual gifts which appeared in the form of a dove, you were always advanced and brought near, till I and my father will come to you. (v.11) Because, behold, the winter is past; the rain has gone and departed; the flowers have appeared on the earth, that is, for behold, the winter of evils and temptations and idolatry has passed from the world in my manifestation in this world. The rain has gone, that is (the rain) of temptations and troubles, on account of death. (v.12) And the flowers have appeared on the earth, that is, the heart which of old was without fruit made the evangelical virtues grow. The time of pruning has arrived; the voice of the turtle-dove has been heard in our land; (v.13) the fig tree has put forth its young figs; the vines put forth the tender grape, they yield a smell, that is, when they who are from the root of Abraham will be cut off because they did not yield fruit, like that (passage): every tree which does not yield fruit is cut down and falls in the fire, (Math. 3:10;
Luke 3:9) which John proclaimed, and he it is who was called by the groom turtle-dove because of his chastity, for he proclaimed in Judah that the groom has come and it is right that he should follow him. He compares the fig tree and vines to the law of Moses, and those precepts and prophecies whose secrets began to take effect when the Messiah came he compared to young because of their imperfection, but when the Messiah appeared thereupon they assumed perfection. Likewise, the tender vines that yield an odor he compared to the prophecies from which the sweet odor of the Messiah's manifestation blew upon us, who, when he had completed these, made them pressed out grapes whose wine excites the teeth and heart of those who perceive them. The groom mentions these (things) to the bride when he wishes to affirm his existence and advent, and that it is not right that she should be ashamed because she believed in him, for, indeed, his types are in the prophets and John preached concerning him. He teaches her again how, and by what, she can draw near and come to him from the things of the world and worldly, and not because the prescriptions of the law were true and testified concerning him should she adhere to these and by them be brought near to him. Arise, come my companion, fair one, my dove, and come now. (v.14) My dove in the shelter of the rock, that is, when you are concealed in the gospel as in a rock, because the things that are in it are a rock upon which structures are reared and they come to me. And he continues: By the side of
the outwork show me thy face, that is, he commands her to show him her face which shines with purity, and the uncovering of the face (confidence), and with these good deeds in which he rejoices; and he continues: Cause me to hear thy voice, that is, the voice of praise and redemption which is heard in the dwelling of the righteous; that is, in the hearts of those that believe; for her voice is sweet to him, he says, like the sweet praise by which he is praised from the heart, he with his father and the holy ghost; likewise the face of purity and chastity is sweet. For thy voice is sweet and thy countenance is beautiful, that is, she replies: if you wish that my countenance should be pleasing to you and you shall hear clearly my voice of praise, then command your hunters, the angels, that they should. (v.15) Capture for us the foxes, the small foxes, that destroy the vineyards, and our vines put forth tender grapes, that is, he calls the demons foxes; she designates them foxes and small when she examines their contemptibility and meanness, and they are not mountains as of old because the power of the cross crushed them and they became contemptible (things);and they hide themselves cunningly in the form of foxes in the caves, that is to say, in the hearts of men, which she calls vineyards; they corrupt them and do not allow that their voice of praise should be clearly heard. But,
she says, whenever these foxes are captured then our vines give forth tender shoots, that is to say,the hearts bear the fruits of virtue from which there blows a sweet odor of the Messiah; it is possible for these tender shoots to become grapes, that is, that they can attain to the sublime disciplines of virtue. And she continues - when can these happen: (v.16) My sister's son is mine and I am his, that is, behold, I have become my sister's son's, and he mine, and there is no division; for he that is united to the Lord is one spirit with him. He that feeds among the lilies, that is, among the splendor and purity and the disciplines which are sweet to him and are reckoned by him as food. Again, he that feeds among the lilies, that is, because of the good pasturage, because of this, upon the sweet meadows of rest and happiness, like among the lilies that are splendid, he feeds those who become disciples to him. (v.17) Until the day will cool and the shadows decline and be moved, that is, she wishes to be fed and guided by him until there will pass from her the heat of the passions and strife, and there will come and cool her the spiritual breath of the spirit which makes her unswerving, and the shadows of darkness he will chase away from her, which are the demons and the (evil) thoughts. Afterwards she asks of him: Turn, be thou like, my kinsman, to a deer, that is, bow down, O Lord, stoop down, as you did also stoop down of old because
of our nature and you destroyed the snakes; so, even now, for the sake of my redemption, be like a deer or a young hart upon the mountains of the abyss, that is, with your assumption of human nature you are like the high mountains, that is to say, the demons you have brought low and the height of these you have cast down, and you have made them an abyss; and now, also, be for my sake to those who contend with me in the abyss, like a deer and a young hart, and destroy and remove them from me.

Afterwards, the prophecy, assuming the character of those who love God and keep his precepts, speaks for them, and teaches them, in the things she says, that they should not endeavor to investigate that incomprehensible nature, neither to see what it is nor how. (v.1) By nights, on my bed, I sought him whom I loved; I sought him, but I did not find him; I called him but he did not answer me, that is, when the soul loves God and keeps his precepts she is at rest like in the night and in bed from the strife of the devil and from the pains. Again, after that knowledge which is conferred by the natural sciences and the writings, when she is at rest and at leisure from these, she prays to see or to attain after these that (higher knowledge) which she loved. But this is not possible for her in this world and not even if she calls to him in prayer, because she asks that which is not given in this world but is kept for the other world. (v.2) I will rise now and go about in the city, in the market place, and in the streets,
and I will seek him whom my soul loved. I sought him but did not find him, that is, she rises now, being surrounded with the thoughts and the sciences, wishing to know, that though he does not grant me to see that, whether among the hosts, the angels, and the souls of the saints are found those which I desire; for an assembly of these she calls city and the ranks and habitations market-places and streets. But the parables and secrets of the writings teach her that not even there is the groom to be found by those who are there just as she who (can not do so) wishes to find him; but she says: (v.3) The watchmen, who go their rounds in the city, found me. Perhaps you have seen him whom my soul loved? that is, the angels who are sent out to the service for the sake of those who are prepared to inherit life, and they guard the soul, the city, from the devil and the demons; and she asks: perhaps he is found by them as even she begs to find. These, however, do not answer concerning this because they do not find him, or because they do not apprehend that what she wishes to desire to attain; and therefore when she has become wise by these she departs from all these and is not rash to ask for the unattainable. (v.4) Till I found him whom my soul loved; I seized him and did not let him go, i.e., she says that she found him whom she loved not by searching and investigation or experience, audacity, and unattainable requests, but by the keeping of the precepts of love, innocence and purity, and such as these. She made them unto herself like a staircase by which she may ascend to him. These, she says, she attained: the secrets, the sciences of the prophets and the apostles. By these she
seized the groom, and she promises not to let go until she brings him into his mother's house and into the chamber of her that conceived, i.e., she does not let go of these things that are his, that is - the doctrines and precepts, by which like of a mother she was born and her heart became the chamber of these. Indeed she does not let him go until she sees him and finds him who dwells in her mind and heart as she loves and desires (it). She does not let him go so that he and his father may come and make for her habitations until the promise which he said (made) is fulfilled: He that loveth me shall be loved of my father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself unto him (John 14:21b); blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God (Math. 5:8). She says again: not because what I desired was rendered me will I now let go of him, but I call to him and praise him, and I do not remove myself from his door till he will enter and dwell in my mind, which was a house and a chamber of that knowledge of which I was born, that I might be his daughter. Afterwards he adjures the angels that they should not allow her love and diligence to cool. (v.5) I have adjured you, O daughter of Jerusalem and so forth, or you stir up the love until he please, i.e., until her desire is fulfilled and also the desire of the groom in her. Afterwards, the character of the friends of the groom enters, i.e., the prophets and the patriarchs, who are wondering at the church and at the transformation that has come to her all at once by the faith in the Messiah; and consequently they say: (v.6) Who is this that comes up from the wilderness, i.e., she goes up from the depths and the thirsty (land), for
there was not in her the spiritual waters of the life-giving teachings of the church of the gentiles, who left her people and forgot her father's house and went up from the earth and earthly (things) to the heavenly (things). Like vines of smoke that yield a fragrance, i.e., vines because of the excellent crop of fruit which are sweeter than those of the palms; smoke because of the sweet fragrance that blows from them. Myrrh and frankincense, i.e., because from it there blows the sweet odor of the death of Jesus which the saints bear in their bodies, with which (myrrh) also is associated, the frankincense in which is borne the type of the resurrection and life and incorruptibility, like Paul said: always bearing the death of Jesus in our bodies that his life also might be made manifest in us' (II Cor. 4:10). Above all the powders of the perfumers, i.e., the virtues by which is named the death unto death in the death of Jesus, (cf. II Cor. 2:16).

They are again saying while teaching: (v.7) Behold, Solomon's bed, that is, the Messiah; the bed, the repose that is in the saints, the Virgin Mary, that queen in whom the saints are at rest as if on a bed. Sixty mighty men are round about her, of the mighty men of Israel. (v.8) All of them are holding swords, learning war; every man has his sword upon his thigh because of the fear of the nights, i.e., the
type of those perfect ones, who because of the power and might made war against the lusts of the devil. They are called mighty men who encircle him round about, who strive for him and on his behalf, so that he is at rest in them and will cause them to rest in him. He says that the mighty men are from Israel, i.e., the perfect ones of the (dispensation) of the law: Adam, Seth, Enoch and the rest of the patriarchs and prophets who descend in the order of succession to the Messiah; for these strove with the spiritual sword of the word and of truth against sin and the devil, who like in darkness draws near to the virtues and throws his spiritual arrows in the deep darkness. These, however, each one of them, holds his spiritual sword upon the thigh, with which they have constantly been armed and have striven, so that they will not be overcome by the terror of the nights, i.e., of the devil, who is darkness and night, and desires to conquer us in the dark; for afterwards these prophesy concerning the church and say: (v.9) King Solomon made himself a throne, i.e., he calls the church a throne because the word was borne upon it in state, because he is at rest in it and dwells in it. He says that it is of the trees of Lebanon, i.e., from the devil, demons, and idolatry, which are symbolized by Lebanon was this wood cut off by the axe of the gospel to be a throne for the Messiah. (v.10) He made his columns of silver, i.e.,the pillars upon which he is set, who are the orthodox teachers, who, by means of their silvery
teaching which is pure and tested in the ground, carry the holy church. The support of his loins is of gold, i.e., the orthodox faith, which like gold brings those that believe in her to incorruptibility and she produces them upon whom the groom supports himself; and it seems to me that these are the holy apostles. The seats of it are purple, i.e., the martyrs, who by their blood were worthy to be the heirs of the Kingdom and upon them the groom sat, and by their blood he made the church firm. In another way, the ascetics who mortified their members of the earth and removed sin from them, who also are like the martyrs. The inside of it is overlaid with stones, i.e., the priests, the ministers, and the rest of the believers who built themselves upon the firm rock of faith and they bound themselves one with each other and with the Messiah. Of the daughters of Jerusalem, i.e., the apostles, the saints, the sons of Jerusalem, who were the cause of this kind of love and the bond of these with each other, because they preached, i.e., the complete love and in their own persons made this manifest in fact. (v.11) Go forth, and see, ye daughters of Zion, King Solomon, i.e., he commands the Jews whom he calls daughters of Zion to depart from sin, from the grudge of their fathers against Jesus, from the world and worldly (things), from the prescriptions of the law and their perceptibility, so that by means of such a departure and the uprightness which results of it (they might see) the things which are to be seen, i.e., in
the church of the nations which believed in the Messiah, because the prophecies concerning him have been fulfilled; as for him, the word calls him King and like one humble and riding upon an ass (Zech. 9:9). Likewise, she calls him Solomon because he is the true peace, who conciliated by his blood the upper and nether realms with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him, i.e., the one that was formed of the people and the gentiles who are round about him, and from all sides, like a crown, they praise and worship. In the day of the gladness of his heart, in the day of his espousals, i.e., this is the day in which he fulfilled his (divine) dispensations for us, the day of the crucifixion, and death, and descent into the Sheol, and his ascent from it, when the souls who believed in him there surround him; and by his resurrection he also gladdened the apostles, and by their mediation he betrothed the church of the nations, and, behold, she rejoices in the faith in him and in his hopes. Be not surprised that the gladness of these, i.e., of the souls of his peoples he made for her, because he is the very cause of these. Likewise, the father who sent him for our redemption he here calls mother, because (he calls the) church bride and him again groom, for it is not absurd that the father should be called mother, since he who was begotten is his in two ways and again was begotten impassively.

Afterwards there enters the character of the Messiah, who speaks to his church and praises it abundantly, so that by means
of the praises he may incite her to faith and love and keeping of his precepts. (v.1) Behold thou art fair my companion, i.e., in that you forgot your people and your father's house and you believed in me and drew near to me. Behold thy eyes are as doves, the teachers who became rich by the spirit and continually make you rich. Beyond the silence, in your teachers and apostles the virtues are great and excel that which is seen. Thy hair is as a flock of these goats that have appeared from Gilead, i.e., the ascetics, the anchorites, those who mortified the members of the earth, those who are her hair, that is to say, the adornment of the bride. They are called her hair because there is nothing in them that lives for the world, for they are dead to themselves and alive for God. He says that this hair is from goats, i.e., because formerly they were the likeness of beasts until (the period of) discipleship; he mentions the mountain of Gilead because of the resemblance of the ascetics to Elijah the Tishbite who was from the mountains of Gilead. (v.2) Thy teeth, i.e., those who crumble the teaching and make it easy that it may be nourishing to those who are in need of spiritual nourishment. He again encourages these and says: Like a flock of these shorn ewes that go up from the washing and all of them are bearing twins and there is not a bereaved one among them, i.e., that they might shear, that is to say, they will cut and shear for those among them whatsoever is material and carnal, and they will always wash in water the soul together with the body; and they will be twofold, that is to say, united and complete in theory and practice, in soul and body. (v.3) Thy lips are
as a thread of scarlet and thy speech is comely, i.e., the faith in the crucifixion and holy communion, and of the body and the blood, by which the lips are sanctified, and the thoughts and the speech of the heart. Again, faith is indicated by means of scarlet and love by means of the thread, which is one and is extended over the church. Like the rind of a pomegranate is the round part of thy cheek beyond thy silence, i.e., this (rind) which by means of its astringency, hardness, and bitterness protects the sweet and perceptual fruits; so also is the evangelical teaching - that gate which is narrow, hard, and bitter to those who have not actually tasted (experienced) impassibility, chastity and the rest of the virtues, which she calls round part of the cheek allegorically, because when the soul is occupied with these it appears excellent to them before everybody and on the lips and speech. But within the silence it is something of another matter for it, which is better: all the good disciplines and the constant intimacy with God, which to the one who sees is revealed secretly and it is done for his sake, so that, he, for his own sake, may reward openly. (v.4) Thy neck is as the tower of David that was built for an armory, i.e., like the perceptual David is high and exalted because God chose him and God made him reign and rule so is the neck of the church, who are the apostles that carry the head of the Messiah
before the peoples and before the Kings; they lift up from the earth and earthly things and bring up to heaven those that become disciples; and it is well known that they appear to them in the likeness of an armory, i.e., battlements. A thousand shields hang upon it, i.e., because there are thousands and myriads that battle with the church, i.e., the devil and the demons, as it is written: Thousands will fall at thy side and myriads at thy right hand,(Ps. 91:7); because of these demons who in thousands and myriads strive with the children of the church, she, therefore, says to her allegorically: he is to you a thousand shields which hang upon you, i.e., a host of angels who surround you and with whom like with shields you are armed. A thousand shields, the completion of the precepts and the perfection of these which is compared to a complete number of the complete ones; when these were hanging upon you, you were not afraid of the arrows of the demons. Of the arrows of the mighty men, i.e., the praises and prayers by which you are to those that strive with you like perceptual arrows. (v.5) Thy two breasts are as two twin fawns of the roe, i.e., the two Testaments with which you nourish your children with spiritual milk are like fawns, because by such teaching you destroy the spiritual snakes, and you destroy and make an end of their teaching and counsels. And she says that these are twins, i.e., in the church; throughout the time (age) the two Testaments were preached and expounded, although the apostles and their teaching
preceding, yet with them and by them the prophets and their words came into the world; as twins that are begotten from one womb, so the cause of these two is God, who from the spiritual womb of his knowledge taught and ordered both of them; and of these he says: These that feed among the lilies, i.e., in splendor and purity and spiritual sweetness of odor. And if one should say that he designates the soul and the body two breasts, since they were created at the same time and one did not precede the other, it is not at all absurd. (v.6) Until the day will cool and the shadows decline, i.e., with these you shall feed and teach and nourish your children O bride, until the day of this world is at an end and sin and the demons will cease, on whose account we were in need of such pasture; then you will be exalted to the light in which you have no need of the two breasts, that is to say, the Testaments. The following text is not in the Septuagint version but is set down in the Symmachus (version): I betake me to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense. In the Peshitto version it is said imperatively: Go to the mountain of myrrh and to the heights of frankincense. Now, if it is said imperatively, then it is the groom who says to the church: come, go,ascend always from the earthly things to the heavenly which are the cause of the mortality of the passions and the rising up from all sin; the reason why he calls it and it is designated hill of frankincense and not mountain is because the rising up from sin is effected in this world and not the resurrection of
the bodies from death. Again, that which the groom says: I betake me to the mountains, etc., may possibly refer to the training of the church and the conversion of her children. But one is able to say that the groom is praising the church with praises such as these because he wishes to teach her to which of her children he goes and among whom he dwells; he says: (v.7) Thou art all fair my companion, and there is no blemish in thee, i.e., yet I betake me to those who became mountains of myrrh, because they were uplifted from the earthly things and mortified themselves, and while yet living in the body they rose from all sin. However, after the groom has praised her and has shown that there is no blemish in her,fearing that she would not advance and ascend to him, either thinking that by means of faith she had been delivered from the conflict of the demons or that she had become unperverted, he, therefore,calls her and says: (v.8) Come from Lebanon, O bride, come from Lebanon, i.e., remember that you have been Lebanon and I cut you down and made you unto me for a throne, and now that you dwell in this world as in Lebanon, it is, therefore, right that you should continually come to me and not remain behind. And he informs her how she can come to him: Thou comest and passest from the summit of faith, i.e., indeed, by this you are able to overcome the world and worldly (things) and conquer the demons, when you are baptised in the name of the father, the son, and the holy ghost, those in whom baptism is perfected. And he continues: From the top of Sanir and Hermon,
i.e., from whence the Jordan issues which indeed is the summit of baptism, on which was revealed the ineffable mystery of the three persons of the Godhead. From the den of the lions and from the mountain of the leopards, i.e., from the midst of those demons who lay in wait for you in the beginning and made you theirs when they caused you to worship idols; but I cut you away from these and freed you from these, and henceforward I remind you of these things, so that I may teach you that although you have come you have not as yet reached that unity with me which frees you from these (demons); and because these, by means of the desires are continually lying in wait for you and wish to remove you from me, I, therefore, call you and say, i.e., come to me always and cleave to those (things) concerning which you were commanded in baptism; because, behold, the lions and leopards are surrounding you, and if you are negligent you will be captured by these. (v.9) Thou hast encouraged us my sister, O bride, thou hast encouraged us, i.e., some say that this verse is as from the character of the angels and prophets who were encouraged by the faith of the church and her disciplines, because they desired it and were afraid that she might not appear as they wish. But that which is said by the Septuagint my sister refers to the Messiah, and he, the Messiah, assuming the character of these (angels and prophets) said: You have encouraged us, i.e., through you, say the angels and the righteous, we see that which is invisible appear in the flesh, and through you we learn the secrets of the extraordinary
wisdom of God. With one of thine eyes, i.e., with that spiritual one which looks at God and the divine (things) and does not see anything of those that are contrary; for they say there are two eyes in the soul: one observes knowledge and virtue, the other which looks upon these carnal things, I mean, the desires and the rest of the worldly (things). With one of the settings of thy neck, in other codices with one chain, for though many are those (things) with which the spiritual neck of the soul is adorned, by which it is exalted above earthly things, yet, says the groom, one of these suffices her, that (one) by which you yoke yourself under my yoke and for my sake you have delivered your neck to the sword for my love. (v.10) How beautiful are thy breasts, more than wine, i.e., the fountain of your teaching with which you purify the disciples, for your teaching is more beautiful than philosophy which is likened to wine. And the smell of thy garments, i.e., your bodily aromas of the powers of the soul, of the virtues. Is better than all the aromas, i.e., better than the virtues which the ancients practised, better than the sacrifices of Noah and Abraham and the law. (v.11) Thy lips drop honeycomb O bride, i.e., discourses, commentaries, interpretations. Honey and milk are under thy tongue, i.e., teaching written in various ways, to those who are in need of growth milk is given, and to
those who are of full growth - wisdom that is discussed by the perfect (is given). And the smell of thy garments is as the smell of frankincense, i.e., your limbs which have died to the world and its desires ascend to God in the likeness of frankincense and sweet incense, because by means of these you rose up from sin. (v.12) My sister, the bride, is a garden enclosed, i.e., he compares her to a garden, that is to say, Paradise, because of its various kinds of ranks which are typified by trees; the righteous are planted in it like an olive tree, and the teachers like palm trees, and the celibates and virgins are like the splendid vine; the leaves of the trees are the sciences, but the fruits are the virtues; and the river that waters and divides itself four-fold is the Messiah, who waters this garden and the tree of life by means of the evangelists. The Messiah calls the garden enclosed because the precepts surround her in the form of a wall; the holy powers also surround her, and it is impossible that she should be pillaged or that the boar of the forest and the beasts of the field should enter it, i.e., the devil and the demons. A fountain that is sealed, that causes to flow water from the life giving teachings and waters the trees that are in it (i.e., garden). And he says that it is sealed, i.e., by purity and holiness are these teachings preserved in the teachers and the disciples. (v.13) Thy shoots, all of them, are a park with the fruit of choice berries, i.e., the words that
are sent forth from your mouth to the recipients of the teachings make a park of pomegranates, that within they might be full of good fruit, that is to say, choice berries, with the sweet sciences, but from without they are protected by something bitter and reddish, which is the narrow gate of the keeping of the precepts. Henna and spikenard plants,(v.14) nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon with all the trees of Lebanon, myrrh and aloes with all the chief spices, i.e., for all these are naturally full of a sweet smell, and each one of these has a certain characteristic that is different from its neighbor, and from all of them is one sweet odor compounded, by which are understood the types of virtue; for all those who, by means of the death of the bodily passions which are likened to myrrh, mortified themselves, are able to enjoy all the virtues, and when man actually accomplishes these he hears the words that are sent forth from the church, from every one of which there blows a smell of knowledge, and virtue, and death likened to the death of Jesus, and of his burial and resurrection. (v.15) A fountain of gardens, i.e., the teaching which waters the souls that became the gardens of the heavenly groom. And a well of living water, i.e., the inscrutable depth of theology out of which its teachers draw life and water those who are thirsty. That flow with vehemence from Lebanon, i.e., they were compared to Lebanon because of their height and loftiness, and he says that these flow with vehemence because they wash away and remove and overwhelm the foul water of the devilish teachings. (v.16) Awake O north, and come O south, i.e., he compared the devil to the north, and
by sayingawake he drives the devil away from his church; to the north he compared the devil, because the wind of the north parches and burns and does not let anything grow like the devil who shrivels and makes an end of the seeds of virtue. Come O south, i.e., he calls the holy spirit to come from the secret places of light, and shine and blow upon those it delights in, and fill with its wondrous gifts, those that became a garden and were worthy of the waters of the teaching and brought forth fruits of virtue. And cool my garden and let the aromas of my fruits flow, for the spirit cooled the souls of the saints and did not allow them to be weary from the heat of the temptations, and makes them so that the spiritual aromas of the sciences should flow from them, sweetening the nostrils of the recipients; for the church asks that the grace of the spirit should be granted, by which is removed from her all the influence of the devil, who is likened to the north because of his darkness and wickedness; the dark places of the world are in the north, and the church asks that she be removed from them; and the breeze of the south, that is to say, of the spirit, he should blow upon her, by which her fruit may grow and there might blow from her the sweet smell of the teaching, so that it may descend and dwell in her. Let my sister's son go down into his garden and eat the fruit of his choice berries, i.e., Jesus, God, who took flesh from that virgin of Judah who is the sister of the church of the nations, and by his descent he will in fact delight in the virtue of this one,
in her alms, in her offerings, which are considered his food, as he has said: My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, (John 4:34), and, indeed, he also ate the fruit of his choice berries, i.e., of the children who are begotten in him and do virtues for his sake.
